targets.name: Gorki
targets.note: Not identified with certainty; probably a heat-and-power plant of the city. Capacity apportioned from the file's total.

targets.name: Balakhna
targets.note: Gorki GRES (NiGRES), peat-fired, about 204 MW since 1933; never bombed directly.

targets.name: Dzerzhinsk
targets.note: Chemical-industry plant; capacity apportioned from the file's total.

targets.name: Yaroslavl (2 plants)
targets.note: Two plants in the file; capacity apportioned.

targets.name: Uglich
targets.note: Hydroelectric, 2 units (8 Dec 1940, 20 Mar 1941), 110 MW. Built by Volgostroy of the NKVD with prisoners of the Volgolag.

targets.name: Komsomolsk
targets.note: The Ivanovo GRES at Komsomolsk; capacity apportioned.

targets.name: Rybinsk
targets.note: Hydroelectric, unit 1 from 18 Nov 1941, unit 2 from 1942; unit 3 only from 15 Aug 1945. Built by Volgostroy with Volgolag prisoners.

targets.name: Stalinogorsk
targets.note: Pre-war at least 300 MW (four 50 MW sets and the USSR's only 100 MW set); blown up 21 Nov 1941, restored in stages from Oct 1942. The 1945 figure is the study's estimate.

targets.name: Kashira
targets.note: 186 MW after restoration (Kopsov p. 90); second stage evacuated to Novosibirsk in 1941, back 1942–43.

targets.name: Shatura
targets.note: 180 MW: 2 × 16 MW and one GE set of 1925–27, 3 × 44 MW of 1933; one 44 MW set to Omsk in 1941, restored 1942.

bases.name: Königsberg
bases.note: Soviet forces reached the Vistula Lagoon on 24 January 1945 and cut East Prussia off; the file of 7 February gives up the Gorki targets for that reason.

bases.name: Danzig / Stolp
bases.note: The file's fallback for the Yaroslavl and Tula groups. Farther Pomerania was cut through to the Baltic in the first days of March; Stolp fell in March, Danzig on 30 March.

bases.name: West of the Oder (Garz, Stargard, Sagan)
bases.note: The file's last resort: from here only the targets round Tula. Sagan fell on 16 February, Stargard on 5 March; Garz on Usedom remained.

bases.name: Berlin area (Rechlin, Oranienburg, Garz)
bases.note: Baumbach: in March 1945 Mistel with greater range were ready to fly from the Berlin area. The US Eighth Air Force bombed Rechlin and Lärz on 10 April 1945.

deliveries.note: The file: 18 delivered by 7 February, the rest 'promised in the course of February'. The study lets them arrive late, at 20 a fortnight, up to the 82 that secondary accounts give for March.

assumptionNotes.serviceable: Share of combinations ready on the day; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.enrouteLoss: Combinations lost to fighters, flak or breakdown over 1,300–1,500 km of enemy territory; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.fogDawn: Koller: at dawn 'ground fog is to be expected very often at this time of year'. The figure is the study's.
assumptionNotes.fogForecast: Waiting a fortnight for a firm forecast; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.findDawn: Koller: finding the target 'can nevertheless be assumed' with experienced illuminator crews and chains of flares. The study does not take 'assumed' as certain.
assumptionNotes.findNight: Koller: success at night only if the targets were 'lit up as bright as day', and the illuminators for that 'are not available'.
assumptionNotes.findLong: 7 February: target finding over 2,500 km 'cannot be solved with the existing pathfinders'.
assumptionNotes.hitFile: The file's own figure: '60 % hit probability of the Mistel'. Baumbach (1949) claimed about 80 %.
assumptionNotes.hitNightFactor: Night attack on point targets without full illumination; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.hitLowTraining: Less fuel for training than the file's 1,400 t; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.returnBaumbach: Reading A, after Baumbach: fuel could be drawn from the Ju 88 on the way out, so the fighter had its own tanks for the return.
assumptionNotes.returnNoTransfer: Reading B, after later accounts: the Fw 190 could not use the Ju 88's fuel, and the fighter had to reach Courland on its own tanks.
assumptionNotes.returnLongLeg: Factor for return legs of more than 1,200 km to Courland; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.illuminators: Ju 88 S 3 and Ju 188 of I./KG 66 and II./KG 4; their number is the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.illuminatorLoss: Loss rate of the illuminator crews; the study's assumption.
assumptionNotes.repairSteam: Months until a destroyed steam set runs again, after the 1941–42 precedents: Kashira supplied Moscow again about five months after its evacuation, Stalinogorsk's first set ran eleven months after the plant was blown up (Kopsov 2015; Mosenergo museum). Those were evacuations and demolitions, not hollow-charge hits.
assumptionNotes.repairHydro: Months for a hydro unit; no wartime precedent, the study's extrapolation.
assumptionNotes.frontDelayMonths: Baumbach: the effects 'could be felt at the front three to four months at the earliest'. The study uses three.
assumptionNotes.longRangeBaumbach: Whether the long-range Mistel would have been ready in March (Baumbach) or not before May (the file of 7 February); the study draws one reading per game and tells you which at the end.

soviet.statsSource: Kopsov (ed.), Moskovskaya energetika v gody Velikoy Otechestvennoy voyny (Moscow 2015), table 3, p. 95.

notes.count: Extreme what-if. The He 177 / Fw 190 'Great Mistel' never flew. A summary of its history (ourairports.biz, after a German secondary source): 100 conversions of He 177 A-3/A-5 planned in August 1944, the order for 98 cancelled in September; the RLM still required two machines; target dates 1 and 15 February 1945; suspended on 28 January 1945 'for lack of coal', abandoned on 12 March. The study lets two to four exist from mid-February.
notes.range: The He 177 had the range to reach every target from the Berlin area; the figure is the study's, for a one-way flight of the lower component.
notes.abort: The He 177's coupled engines were notoriously prone to fire; share of combinations that turn back or are lost before the target, the study's assumption.
notes.hitP: The file's 60 % for the Ju 88 Mistel, carried over; no figure exists for the He 177 combination.
notes.unitsPerHit: A heavier charge than the Ju 88's; the study lets one hit destroy up to two generating sets. An assumption, nothing more.
notes.find: Beyond the 'Sonne' beacons and without a pathfinder solution for 1,600–2,000 km, as the file says of the long-range Mistel.
